items.summary: LMCache's multiprocess (distributed) mode opens an unauthenticated ZeroMQ ROUTER socket where msgpack extension code 1 is passed to pickle.loads before any handler validation, letting an unauthenticated remote attacker execute arbitrary code — as root in official container images — with a single ZMQ message. Discovered by JFrog Security Research.

Splunk Enterprise (10.4.x before 10.4.3, 10.2.x before 10.2.7) exposes the Patroni REST API on search head cluster members without authentication for critical configuration operations, allowing any network-reachable attacker to execute attacker-controlled OS commands. Advisory SVD-2026-1001.

LMCache through 0.5.5 contains an unauthenticated remote code execution flaw in its /run_script endpoint: remote attackers can post scripts that execute Python code and OS commands as the LMCache process, recovering real builtins through the injected FastAPI app object to bypass the guarded __import__. Disclosed by VulnCheck.

IBM Langflow OSS 1.0.0 through 1.12.2 allows a remote unauthenticated attacker to execute arbitrary code via improper neutralization of special elements used in an OS command (CWE-94 code injection). Fixed in 1.12.3 per the IBM advisory.

wolfSSH (≤1.5.0, fixed in 1.6.0) does not validate that the ECDSA curve identifier in the KEXDH_REPLY host key blob matches the algorithm negotiated during key exchange, letting an active man-in-the-middle substitute a host key on a different curve it controls and pass signature verification — a forged server key. Requires lax host-key checking on the client.
